verdict.rationale: The evidence shows Reader can render pages in headless Chrome (`x-engine: browser`), wait for a selector (`x-wait-for-selector`), and control response timing. None of these is scripted interaction: there is no documented way to click, fill inputs, or scroll before content is returned. Waiting for an element is an adjacent control, not the capability itself, so it earns no credit.

support.subject: As a developer, I can script page interactions like clicking, filling inputs, and scrolling before content is returned
